purpose: Evidence about the magnitude of pricing losses and credibility of demand; no source is evidence of GadgetPickup algorithm adoption.

sources.title: Dynamic Pricing under Competition on Online Marketplaces: A Data-Driven Approach
sources.verified: Random assignment of more than 5000 used books per strategy, three months, equal repricing frequency. Table 8 reports 23.1 percent higher accumulated profit for S3.
sources.interpretation: Suggestive analogous professional used-goods market. An improvement over incumbent performance is not an upper bound on regret versus the best policy. The tested policy and profit definition differ from the narrow Swappa menu.

sources.title: Analytics for an Online Retailer: Demand Forecasting and Price Optimization
sources.verified: Rue La La field experiment estimates 9.7 percent higher revenue, with a 90 percent interval of 2.3 to 17.8 percent.
sources.interpretation: Revenue, not profit or regret; fashion flash sales differ from used phones. Cannot calibrate a 5 or 10 percent profit allowance.

sources.title: How Effective Is Suggested Pricing? Experimental Evidence from an E-Commerce Platform
sources.verified: Publisher abstract: randomized suggested prices on Mercari; 30 percent change in suggestions induces 5 percent same-direction listing-price change. Lower suggestions improve sale likelihood and seller revenue.
sources.access_limit: Abstract accessed; no numerical structural demand elasticity extracted from the full paper.
sources.interpretation: Suggestive experimental support for the direction of a price response in used-goods sales; no transferable GadgetPickup elasticity or profit-efficiency bound. Publication in 2026 does not establish 2023 software availability or adoption.

sources.title: Can I offer a lower price or negotiate?
sources.verified: Accepted buyer offers can be implemented by editing the public listing price before purchase. The current FAQ expressly excludes Enterprise Seller listings from this mechanism.
sources.interpretation: A possible source of price-sale simultaneity; current FAQ does not establish its prevalence for GadgetPickup in 2023. Prior archived research notes document a 2023 GadgetPickup offer/refusal exchange, not an accepted negotiated sale.
